source.title: OthelloGPT learned a bag of heuristics

record.tranche_reason: The post reports neuron-level results about Othello board-state rules and legal-move patterns, but does not test whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs or any other listed version of the polysemanticity claim.
record.gate_note: The post discusses neuron functions and mentions superposition as a possible future direction, but does not measure polysemanticity, unrelated input responses, or the rate of coherent versus mixed-purpose neurons. The rows below record relevant neuron-function findings; they do not test a listed claim version.
record.test_reason: The post reverse-engineers Othello-GPT's board-state and legal-move computation via individual neurons (decision-rule neurons, board pattern neurons, clock neurons). It never measures whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs, nor the share of polysemantic neurons, nor causes of polysemanticity. Board pattern neurons respond to unions of patterns that all make one move legal, which is one job, not a mixture. Superposition is mentioned only as speculation about smaller models. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors' best guess is that Othello-GPT computes board state and legal moves through a bag of many independent, localized heuristics. They note they cannot rule out an additional succinct algorithm.
record.recipe_differences: The post does not use or compare the original sources’ methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported neuron effects differ by layer: pattern-neuron ablations in layers 3–6 lower target-square probability on average, while layer 7 ablations raise it.

fits_no_version.finding: Specific neurons implement localized conjunctive board-update rules: L1N421 updates B4+C4+D4, gated by L0N377. The rule does not generalize to translations across the board.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In Othello-GPT, individual MLP neurons implement localized, position-specific heuristic rules.

fits_no_version.finding: Hundreds of mid-to-late MLP neurons classify unions of board patterns that make a single move legal (F1>0.99). Ablating them lowers the target move's probability in layers 3-6 and raises it in layer 7.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In Othello-GPT, many MLP neurons act as classifiers for groups of board patterns tied to one legal move and causally affect move probabilities.

record.problems: The post describes a small mechanistic case study and says the board-state circuit was examined across 50 games but not checked for exclusive use. It gives no uncertainty estimates for the reported pattern-neuron results. The authors also caution that Othello-GPT may not represent typical language models.
record.rows_left_out: Board-state probe visualizations, logit-lens observations, and clock-neuron discussion were omitted because they concern board-state or move-prediction computations rather than neuron responses to unrelated inputs.

untested.parts: All; Othello-GPT is a game-move transformer, and no share of neurons responding to unrelated tokens is reported.
All; superposition is only speculated about for smaller models.
All; no architecture or activation comparisons.
All; no canonical polysemantic neurons are re-examined.
All; the F1 thresholds (0.99 vs 0.9) change pattern coverage, not polysemanticity judgments.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T6/discusses classification is right. All rows correctly link to none. Clock neurons, which fire by move number, are also outside the versions. The post's speculation that a smaller model would be forced into superposition is not a test of V3.

relation.reason: Only the Future Work section touches the topic: it speculates that a smaller model might learn features in superposition. Nothing tests the claim.

tranche.reason: The post reverse-engineers Othello-GPT circuits (decision-rule, board-pattern and clock neurons). It never measures whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs, how common polysemantic neurons are, or what causes polysemanticity. It also does not use that finding as a tool.

source_check.notes: All 8 rows match the text. None of them bears on any version: Othello-GPT is a game-move transformer, and no unrelated-input test is reported. The 610 count is filtered to single-move neurons (footnote 7). Layer 3-6 numbers are interpreted as layers 3-5 in the source. In r6 the source does not say whether 'pattern neurons in layers 0-2' means causally relevant ones.
